info.title: Sandcrab native service
info.description: Isolated commands, persistent sessions, durable volumes, files and command events. Unix sockets require the configured peer UID; optional loopback TCP requires a bearer token on every request. The empty HTTP security alternative applies only to authenticated Unix transport. Sequential HTTP/1.1 exchanges follow Connection: close; consume a complete chunked event response before reuse. Server epochs guard new operations; retained volume and upload identities have separate lifetimes. TCP provides no TLS or listener identity attestation.

servers.description: Replace with the configured literal loopback address and port; bearer authentication is required.
Host placeholder for Unix socket transport; authentication is the configured operating-system peer UID.

200.description: Server epoch, capabilities and available profile limits.

parameters.name: capability
parameters.description: Return only this capability and its referenced schemas. Prefer this bounded view for model tools.

post.description: An identical request ID and body reuses a run within this server epoch. Changed arguments conflict. Forgetting ends replay protection; never reuse a forgotten ID. Unknown outcomes after restart must not be silently rerun.
Requests cancellation without claiming containment. Poll for the terminal state.
Releases a terminal result and its replay identity. Running and closing records cannot be forgotten.

Create an isolated persistent bash session. Repeating the same ID and request returns that session, including its terminal state; different arguments conflict. Poll until ready before submitting a command.

get.description: Read the session state. A connection does not own the session lifetime.

post.description: Admit one command while ready. Commands retain shell state and files. Concurrent commands are refused. Read, cancel and forget the returned command through /v1/runs/{id}. Cancellation, timeout, output overflow or shell exit ends the whole session; it is never silently reset.
Extend a live session from the current time, within its profile TTL. Expired sessions cannot be revived.
Stop the whole session, including background processes. Poll until closed, expired or failed. Closing means containment or cleanup is unconfirmed and admission stays held until restart.
Forget a closed, expired or failed session. Retained command records are independent and must be forgotten separately. Never reuse this session ID.

get.description: List at most 100 durable records in UUID order. Concurrent changes are not a snapshot. Continue with nextAfter.

post.description: Create empty persistent storage or a reflink clone of an unattached ready volume. Same ID and normalized plan replay across daemon restarts, including failure or deletion. An unknown ID requires the current serverId. Different plans conflict. Limits may only be lowered. A clone must use the same execution UID/GID as its source. Only one storage mutation runs at a time.
Explicitly delete an unattached ready volume. Deletion intent is durable before data removal; deleted tombstones remain replayable. closing requires restart and reconciliation.
Forget only a deleted or failed record after its data is absent. Ends durable replay protection. Never reuse this client ID.

get.description: Up to ten records in UUID order. Continue with nextAfter.

post.description: Register an upload plan. The ID binds its digest excluding serverId; changed plans conflict. Existing IDs replay across daemon restarts when metadata is retained. Unknown IDs require the current serverId and a live session. Waiting records hold no workspace. Never reuse a forgotten ID.

put.description: Stream exactly the registered byte count and SHA-256. Content-Length is required; chunked bodies are refused. Expect: 100-continue is supported after admission. The private staging helper validates the full stream before any workspace mutation. Raw replaces one file; tar installs an ordinary directory tree. replace=false refuses an existing destination. Optional freezing covers publication only and always ends before the response. The response closes the connection, including replay and refusal before body consumption. A lost response requires inspecting this ID.

post.description: Cancel waiting or active ingestion. Publication is not rolled back; inspect the returned record until settled. An uncertain cleanup holds ownership.
Release a waiting or terminal record only when no stage remains. End replay protection; never reuse this ID.

Capture a raw file or an ordinary tar of a directory, then thaw before sending bytes. Symlinks in tar remain links and are never followed. The Content-Length and quoted SHA-256 ETag describe immutable captured bytes. Complete delivery confirms stage cleanup; a failure may truncate the body. Snapshots are request-scoped and are not retained for reconnect. This response closes its connection.

200.description: Snapshot bytes; validate both declared length and ETag before installing locally.

get.description: Observe a finite run or session command without starting, cancelling or forgetting it. A state event precedes stdout/stderr blocks and one result event. Output order is preserved within each stream; cross-stream order is unspecified. Every complete event carries an id cursor. Reconnect explicitly with Last-Event-ID to continue after its bytes. The result event is published only after containment is confirmed; EOF, heartbeat or an error event does not imply completion. Retain the run until observation finishes. Slow readers lose only their subscription. Maximum observation time is 350 seconds; an unfinished run remains inspectable. Requests and non-stream responses still require fixed HTTP lengths.

200.description: Chunked SSE. Each data field is one JSON value; the event field selects its schema. An id is an opaque resume cursor. Comments are heartbeats. Consume the zero chunk before reusing the connection.

get.description: Read per-command call metadata. Only the request stream carries payloads. Replied records confirm file publication, not guest consumption or an outside business commit. Pending calls become abandoned when their command ends; records last until the run is forgotten or the daemon restarts. HOST_CALLS_DISABLED means the profile did not enable this facility.

post.description: Publish an opaque reply to one pending call. Identical replies return their existing receipt without republication, including after command completion; different reply bytes conflict. Cancellation or closure refuses a new reply. An uncertain publication returns CALL_REPLY_UNCERTAIN and cancels the command; an identical retry stays uncertain. Reply handles are allocated by the daemon, so guest-selected IDs cannot target a later command generation. JSON bodies have a 131072-byte bound; decoded payloads have a 65536-byte bound.

get.description: Observe unresolved calls with state, call, result and error events. The daemon interprets neither request nor reply bytes and runs no host handler. Observations do not claim work: callers authorize requests and reconcile duplicate IDs before repeating outside effects. Reconnect explicitly without a cursor to re-offer pending calls, or with Last-Event-ID to continue after delivered requests. Replies already recorded before selection are skipped; in-flight observations may be stale. Host-call and output streams share observer capacity and the 350-second observation deadline. Each complete frame is at most 131072 bytes and may span HTTP chunks. Result requires confirmed command containment; an error or EOF does not prove completion.

hostCalls.description: Operator-enabled opaque host calls; false by default.

available.description: False requires operator reconciliation and daemon restart before mutations.
False requires reconciliation and daemon restart before file mutations.

activeStreams.description: A concurrent snapshot, not a reservation.

command.description: Executable argv, not shell text. First item is nonempty; arguments contain no NUL. Each is at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes, all arguments at most 16384 bytes.

timeoutMillis.description: Omit or null to use the profile. May only lower its timeout.

outputLimitBytes.description: Omit or null to use the profile. Combined raw stdout/stderr byte bound; may only lower the profile limit.

sessionId.description: Present for commands executed in a persistent session.

stdout.description: UTF-8 text with invalid sequences replaced.

stderr.description: UTF-8 text with invalid sequences replaced.

ttlMillis.description: Cannot exceed the selected profile lifetime.

volumeId.description: Optional ready volume mounted at /workspace exclusively until confirmed session cleanup. Omit for an ephemeral workspace.

command.description: Bash source, at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes, without NUL.

expiresAtMillis.description: Wall-clock estimate of expiry; enforcement uses a monotonic deadline.

code.description: Opening or cleanup failure, including VOLUME_IN_USE, VOLUME_NOT_READY, VOLUME_PROFILE_MISMATCH or CONTAINMENT_UNCONFIRMED.

byteLimit.description: XFS charged-byte quota, at most the advertised storage maximum; sparse logical lengths are not charged blocks.

inodeLimit.description: Inode quota including the managed parent and data directories, at most the advertised maximum.

planDigest.description: SHA-256 of the normalized creation plan, excluding the transport serverId.

busy.description: Exclusively attached to a session or held as a clone source.

path.description: Relative workspace path; at most 64 components, each at most 255 UTF-8 bytes. Empty, dot, parent and backslash components and control characters are refused. Parents must exist.

mode.description: Ordinary permission bits; default 0644 for raw files or 0755 for the target tar directory. Archive member permissions lose special bits and ownership comes from the profile.

path.description: Relative workspace path; at most 64 components, each at most 255 UTF-8 bytes. Empty, dot, parent and backslash components and control characters are refused. Parents must exist.

publication.description: committed confirms synchronized publication; unknown never authorizes another write.

path.description: A relative file path for raw; a relative directory path or . for tar.

EventCursor.description: Opaque Last-Event-ID from a complete event. Binds one retained run incarnation and the next raw stdout/stderr byte offsets. Never reuse it for another run or after forgetting.

offset.description: Starting raw byte offset in the named stream.

base64.description: One nonempty block of at most 4096 exact bytes; no UTF-8 boundary is assumed.

sessionId.description: Present for commands executed in a persistent session.
Present for commands executed in a persistent session.

id.description: Daemon-allocated reply handle, separate from the guest request ID.

requestId.description: Guest-generated correlation ID printed by the in-sandbox CLI.

base64.description: Canonical padded base64 of at most 65536 opaque bytes; empty bytes are allowed.

HostCallCursor.description: Opaque command incarnation and delivered request sequence. A cursor does not acknowledge outside effects.

Resources.description: Optional lower hard caps. Values cannot exceed the selected profile. Memory must meet its minimumMemoryBytes; 100 CPU percent is one CPU.

Volume202.description: Durable operation accepted; poll the volume ID

Upload200.description: Retained identity or current outcome. A failed or unknown outcome is not a successful write.

Upload201.description: Identity registered; send content only while waiting.

Error401.description: TCP credentials are missing or incorrect. AUTH_REQUIRED closes the connection before body admission or 100 Continue.

bearerAuth.description: Required on every TCP request, including discovery and streaming. The no-HTTP-credential alternative applies only to Unix sockets authenticated by peer UID.
